developments.title: After-hours technology losses coexist with a modest early futures recovery
developments.facts: Public IBD coverage reports renewed technology weakness and Apple falling after earnings. Its original publication was November 2 at 21:53:32 UTC; the observed version was updated November 3 at 00:35:36 UTC. The full early Tuesday Trading Economics narrative reports Apple and Palantir down nearly 3% after hours, while broad US futures edge higher. These are distinct measures. Late Monday Reuters explicitly says technology-investment concerns can support USD haven demand. This challenges a blanket claim that US-origin equity stress necessarily weakens the dollar. No private flows or matched Fed repricing are observed.

developments.title: Euro-area manufacturing holds up while German retail disappoints
developments.facts: Final October euro-area manufacturing PMI was 52.7 versus flash 52.4 and September 52.9. Germany expanded, France contracted; input and selling-price pressure remained strong. Separately German September retail sales fell 2.0% m/m against Reuters +0.4%. The sector and period differences matter: factory resilience does not erase weak household demand. Upcoming October euro-area inflation around 4.0% is a Reuters forecast, not an actual.

developments.title: ECB survey package: higher energy inflation, contained second rounds and a pre-meeting one-hike median
developments.facts:
Official SPF headline forecasts 2026/27/28 = 3.0/2.6/2.0 vs 2.7/2.2/2.0; core 2.4/2.5/2.2, revisions 0/+0.2/+0.1; 2031 headline 2.0 anchored. Wage forecast 3.3/3.1/2.8, mild near up revisions but later deceleration; limited second round effects. Growth 1.0/1.3/1.3, chiefly mechanical prior strength; risks down.

SMA collected Oct 12-14, 69 respondents, median DFR 2.50 Oct, 2.75 Dec flat through 2027Q4, 2.50 early 2028, 2.25 late 2028. This is survey vintage not postmeeting market pricing or ECB commitment. 64 company contacts Sept 28-Oct 7 report moderate Q3/Q4 growth, AI/electrification/defence strength but weak retail/process industries/construction; declining headcounts, productivity helps services.

Stronger Q3 selling prices with some Q4 moderation; ~90% consumer-facing firms report only partial/limited pass-through. Expected wages 3.0 in 26/2.9 in 27, 40% see higher wage demand risk vs 20 but majority no notable effect. No claim Europe has no AI investment; sources explicitly show it. One coherent survey-stage review, not independent vote count.

Housing demand was -27% versus expected -12%; consumer-credit standards tightened 14%. Higher rates and risk perceptions drove restriction; AI-infrastructure loan demand is a positive offset. These are bank survey balances, not credit volumes or realised GDP. The survey was conducted September 21 to October 6 and is dated background, not a new October 29 release.
